extracted.intended_audience: Users of the Metamath program (proof authors, maintainers, and learners of Metamath)
extracted.subtask_description: Hands-on command reference and usage guidance for the Metamath program, especially for creating, displaying, verifying, and exporting proofs and database files via the Proof Assistant and MM> prompt. Covers command syntax, qualifiers, warnings, and recommended workflows (save/log/verify).

rubrics_metrics.name: echo on usage
rubrics_metrics.description: et echo on command will cause command lines to be echoed with any abbreviations expanded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use while learning Metamath commands to see the exact command that an abbreviated input corresponds to.

rubrics_metrics.name: set scroll mode
rubrics_metrics.description: set scroll prompted or set scroll continuous — prompted mode pauses after each full screen; continuous scrolls without pausing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default is prompted mode. Choose continuous for uninterrupted long listings, prompted for interactive reading.

rubrics_metrics.name: set width for screen and rewrap behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: set width number — Metamath assumes a 79-character screen width by default (61 chars used for LaTeX output examples).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust for your terminal/printer width. Larger width helps when logging proofs for wide printers; smaller width may be necessary on some terminals. The /rewrap qualifier honors the set width parameter when reformatting comments/statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: set height for paging
rubrics_metrics.description: set height number — Metamath assumes 24 lines by default and pauses when that many lines have been displayed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Change to match terminal height so paging and prompts behave correctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: beep command caveat
rubrics_metrics.description: beep produces a beep; b is an abbreviation for beep.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If b is typed immediately after a paged display ('Press <return> for more...'), the b will back up to the previous page instead of beeping; use the full 'beep' in that case.

rubrics_metrics.name: using more vs OS commands
rubrics_metrics.description: more filename displays an ascii file (simple convenience).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This builtin is limited; for more powerful file viewing, execute your OS's command by enclosing the line in quotes to run it from Metamath (e.g., 'dir' on VAX/VMS). Note: Mac OS prior to X lacks a CLI so this feature won't work there.

rubrics_metrics.name: operating system command execution
rubrics_metrics.description: A line enclosed in single or double quotes will be executed by the OS command line interface.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trailing quote is optional for convenience. Useful for invoking shell commands from the MM> prompt where supported.

rubrics_metrics.name: database size model / limits
rubrics_metrics.description: There are no fixed pre-defined limits on labels, tokens, statements; Metamath uses 32-bit (or 64-bit on 64-bit CPUs) indices and dynamic allocation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generally unlimited within system memory constraints; be aware of platform word-size behaviors.

rubrics_metrics.name: file creation/appending and backup renaming policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Commands that create new files will not overwrite an existing filename; the existing file is renamed filename~1, filename~1 to filename~2, etc., up to filename~9 which is deleted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This helps recovery but can clutter directories; clean up ~n files occasionally. /no versioning (write source) prevents creating ~n backups.

rubrics_metrics.name: read command behavior and /verify
rubrics_metrics.description: read file-name [/verify] reads a Metamath source file and any includes; statement syntax is checked but proofs are not unless /verify is used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoting filenames with slashes is necessary on Unix; if prompted for filename, do not put quotes. /verify slows reading but verifies proofs as the database is read in.

rubrics_metrics.name: write source reformatting and qualifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: write source filename [/rewrap] [/split] [/keep includes] [/no versioning] writes the database to a file with optional rewrapping, splitting included files, preserving includes, and disabling version backups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: /rewrap reformats statements/comments per set.mm conventions (respects set width); does not modify <HTML>...</HTML> blocks nor proofs. Use save proof * /compressed to reformat proofs. /split writes included files separately; /keep includes prevents deletion/renaming of included files; /no versioning skips ~n backups.

rubrics_metrics.name: show settings / memory
rubrics_metrics.description: show settings shows various parameters; show memory shows remaining memory (not meaningful on modern OS with virtual memory).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use show settings to inspect configured timeouts/limits relevant to proof assistant operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: show labels matching and qualifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: show labels label-match [/all] [/linear] lists labels of $a and $p statements matching label-match; * matches zero or more characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: /all includes $e and $f statement labels; /linear displays one label per line useful for scripting.

rubrics_metrics.name: show statement modes and one-qualifier rule
rubrics_metrics.description: show statement label-match [qualifier] displays information about labeled statements. Only one qualifier at a time is allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Qualifiers include /comment (include preceding comment), /full (complete info including $e and $f statements), /tex, /simple_tex, /html, /alt_html, /brief_html, /brief_alt_html. /tex writes to opened LaTeX file; /simple_tex avoids LaTeX macros for easier manual edits.

rubrics_metrics.name: search syntax and qualifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: search label-match "symbol-match" [/all] [/comments] [/join] searches $a and $p statements matching label-match for occurrences of symbol-match; $* matches any symbol sequence; symbols must be separated by whitespace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quotes may be single or double. /all searches $e and $f too. /comments searches the comment immediately preceding each matched statement (case-insensitive arbitrary string) and /join prepends $e hypotheses for searching; see help search for ? and $? wildcard details.

rubrics_metrics.name: show proof display modes and qualifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: show proof label-match [qualifiers] displays proofs in various formats; default shows only logical steps in indented format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key qualifiers: /essential (default — trim $f hypotheses), /all (do not trim $f), /from_step, /to_step, /tree_depth, /reverse, /renumber (with /essential), /tex (writes LaTeX to opened tex file), /lemmon (Lemmon non-indented style with explicit step refs), /start_column (for /lemmon), /normal (normal source-file format), /compressed (compressed source format), /statement_summary (summarize used statements), /detailed_step (show details of single step). Some qualifiers are mutually exclusive (e.g., /normal and others). Use /essential to focus on essential proof structure; use /compressed or /normal to get proof suitable for inclusion in source files.

rubrics_metrics.name: show usage and recursive option
rubrics_metrics.description: show usage label-match [/recursive] lists statements whose proofs make direct reference to the specified statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: /recursive also includes statements whose proofs ultimately depend on the specified statement (indirect dependencies).

rubrics_metrics.name: show trace_back options and counting
rubrics_metrics.description: show trace_back label-match [/essential] [/axioms] [/tree] [/depth number] [/count_steps] lists all statements that the proof depends on with options to restrict to $e hypotheses, list only axioms, display as tree, or limit depth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: /count_steps counts the number of steps back to axioms; if /essential is specified, expansions of syntax-construction hypotheses are not counted.

rubrics_metrics.name: verify proof command and /syntax_only
rubrics_metrics.description: verify proof label-match [/syntax_only] verifies proofs of specified statements; wildcards permitted; verify proof * verifies all proofs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: /syntax_only checks syntax and RPN stack violations only (does not check correctness) — useful for detecting incomplete proofs with ?'s. Note: read then verify proof * ensures database free of Metamath language errors but does not check comment markup; use verify markup * for markup checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: verify markup checks
rubrics_metrics.description: verify markup label-match [/date_skip] [/top_date_skip] [/file_skip] [/verbose] checks comment markup and adopted informal conventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It error-checks latexdef/htmldef/althtmldef in $t comments, '...', ~ label, bibliographic markups, $p vs $a ax/ax- content matching, and date consistency of "(Contributed by...), (Revised by...), (Proof shortened by...)" tags. /date_skip skips date checks; /top_date_skip checks all but the top-of-database version date; /file_skip skips checks that require external files; /verbose lists axXXX vs ax-XXX matches.

rubrics_metrics.name: save proof reformat and persistence behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: save proof label-match [/normal] [/compressed] reformats a proof in-place in the source buffer in normal or compressed format; not permanently saved until write source is invoked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: /normal saves as sequence-of-labels format; /compressed reduces storage (see Appendix B). Use write source after save proof to persist changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: must add $p with ? before using Proof Assistant
rubrics_metrics.description: Before using the Proof Assistant, add a $p statement containing the statement to be proved with a single ? as its proof (e.g., equid $p x = x $= ? $.) then use prove label.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof Assistant (MM-PA>) works by constructing the proof backward using assign and related commands. The assistant enforces legal operations given known information but does not discover proofs for you; it helps to practice by reconstructing existing proofs manually first.

rubrics_metrics.name: proof-creation workflow and safety recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Proofs are created working backwards via assign commands; a proof is complete when all steps are assigned and unified and all $d restrictions are verified after saving.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use undo liberally, keep a log file (open log), save frequently (save new_proof then write source). To recover from bad unifications use delete floating_hypotheses then initialize all then unify all /interactive. After completing a proof, run save new_proof followed by verify proof label to verify $d restrictions (Proof Assistant version may not enforce $d during construction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof Assistant step commands (assign/let/unify/initialize/delete/match/minimize_with/improve/etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proof Assistant provides commands: show new_proof (with /unknown,/not_unified), assign (step label with /no_unify and first/last/negative indexing), let variable/let step to force symbol sequences, unify step/all (/interactive), initialize step/all (de-unify), delete step/all/floating_hypotheses (dangerous warnings), match step/all, minimize_with, improve (with /depth, /no_distinct), undo/redo, save new_proof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: assign refuses unifiable-incompatible statements; let commands can force sequences but may require recovery steps if incorrect; unify all /interactive prompts for ambiguous uniﬁcations; initialize and delete can recover from errors but delete all is dangerous; delete floating_hypotheses is safer. improve fills in steps automatically but its /depth grows search exponentially — save work and be cautious. /no_distinct skips trial statements with $d requirements, possibly missing legal assignments. Use set search_limit and set unification_timeout to control searches. match all can produce many matches and is currently limited; prefer search for locating candidate theorems.

rubrics_metrics.name: set unification_timeout tuning
rubrics_metrics.description: set unification_timeout number controls how long the Proof Assistant will try to compute uniﬁcations (available outside PA but affects PA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uniﬁcation time may grow exponentially with many temporary variables. Increase when willing to wait (default 100000; increasing to 1000000 can help difficult cases). Check current value with show settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: set empty_substitution semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: set empty_substitution on|off toggles whether variables may be substituted with empty symbol sequences in Proof Assistant mode (default off).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some formal systems (e.g., Deduction Rule implementations or MIU system) require empty substitutions; leave off for set.mm. Note: outside of Proof Assistant, verify proof always allows empty substitutions. Turning this on increases ambiguous uniﬁcations.

rubrics_metrics.name: set search_limit for improve
rubrics_metrics.description: set search_limit number sets when the improve command gives up (available outside PA but affects PA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Increase to let improve search harder; show settings reveals current value. Be careful: deeper searches may explode in time/memory.

rubrics_metrics.name: save new_proof persistence and cautions
rubrics_metrics.description: save new_proof label [/normal] [/compressed] saves the in-progress proof into the source buffer; not permanent until write source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an incomplete proof is saved, user let assignments and manual uniﬁcation choices are lost; improve all before save new_proof to retain as much information as possible. Use /compressed for smaller storage.

rubrics_metrics.name: creating LaTeX output prerequisites and workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: To generate LaTeX output, the database must include necessary typesetting info ($t token mappings); show statement and show proof have /tex and /simple_tex qualifiers that write to an opened LaTeX file (open tex).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical workflow: read set.mm; open tex example.tex; show statement ... /tex; show proof ... /tex; close tex; then pdflatex example.tex to produce PDF. open tex has /no_header to suppress standard header/trailer. Mapping to LaTeX symbols is defined in $t comments (Appendix A).

rubrics_metrics.name: creating HTML output and qualifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: show statement label-match /html creates HTML pages (label-match.html) for $a and $p statements; wildcards produce mmdefinitions.html and mmascii.html in addition. /alt_html uses althtmldef, /brief_html produces concise definition/theorem lists suitable for copy/paste, /brief_alt_html is the alternative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Database must include typesetting info. Use ?* as label-match to produce only the two auxiliary files. /alt_html uses althtmldef entries instead of htmldef.
